chunks: The limit for the postnatal period of refraining from salat (prayer) became eighteen days, because the minimum of menstruation is three days, its maximum is ten days, and its middle is five days. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made for the postnatal woman the days of the minimum of menstruation, its middle, and its maximum.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), from which the postnatal woman refrains during nifas
key_terms.النُّفَسَاءِ: women in the state of postnatal bleeding
key_terms.الْحَيْضِ: menstruation, used here as the basis for calculating the nifas limit
key_terms.ثَمَانِيَةَ عَشَرَ يَوْمًا: eighteen days, the stated limit for postpartum refraining from salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: Why is the limit of postpartum bleeding for refraining from salat (prayer) set at eighteen days in this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh basis for setting the upper limit of the postnatal period of refraining from salat (prayer) at eighteen days. It explains this by combining the minimum, middle, and maximum durations of menstruation as a juridical rationale for nifas.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
'The limit for the postnatal period of refraining from prayer has been set at eighteen days because the minimum duration of menstruation is three days, the maximum is ten days, and the average is five days.
Thus, Allah (swt), the Exalted, has designated the days of postnatal bleeding (nifas) to correspond with the minimum, average, and maximum days of menstruation.'
